article.ref: Laura K. Lawless, Lawless French, Articles, Definite articles, and Partitive article, lawlessfrench.com, read 2026-10-09
article.note: The definite article agrees in gender and number. Le and la become l’ before a vowel or a mute h. À contracts with le and les, and de contracts with le and les. À la, à l’, de la, and de l’ do not contract. Du is both the masculine partitive and the contraction of de + le. Des is the indefinite plural, the partitive plural, and the contraction of de + les. The school rule reduces des to de before a preceding adjective in the plural, and usage also keeps des. That choice is not asked. In a negative sentence the indefinite and the partitive usually become de. That choice is not asked either.

pronouns.ref: Laura K. Lawless, Lawless French, Subject pronouns, Direct objects, Indirect objects, and Stressed pronouns, lawlessfrench.com, read 2026-10-09
pronouns.note: Me, te, le, and la elide before a vowel or a mute h: m’, t’, l’. Lui as an indirect object is masculine or feminine. Lui as a stressed pronoun is masculine, and the feminine stressed form is elle. Nous and vous have one spelling for the subject, the direct object, the indirect object, and the stressed form, so the place shows the use. The reflexive series is me, te, se, nous, vous, se. It is not asked. Y and en are not in this table.

verbs.note: Être takes avoir in the passé composé. Le Conjugueur prints the participle été four times, with no feminine ending. The future stem is ser-. Je serai is future. Je serais is conditional and is not entered.

The passé composé cells are the forms with no agreement, which is the agreement with the subject. The participle eu takes e and s when it agrees with a preceding direct object. Those agreeing forms are stored under participe_passe and are not asked. The future stem is aur-.

Le Conjugueur calls this the general pattern of verbs in -er. The auxiliary is avoir, so the passé composé does not agree with the subject. For an -er verb, the singular and the third person plural of the present subjunctive are spelled like the present indicative, and the nous and vous forms are spelled like the imparfait. The clause shows which is meant. Le Robert, Dico en ligne, « Subjonctif », dictionnaire.lerobert.com, read 2026-10-09

Le Conjugueur: verbs in -ir that form the present participle in -issant. The nous and vous forms of the imparfait and of the present subjunctive are spelled alike. The present and the present subjunctive also share finissent. The imperfect subjunctive, which is not entered, spells que je finisse like the present subjunctive.

Le Conjugueur: the general pattern of verbs in -dre, except prendre. The third person singular of the present is vend, with no added letter. The future stem drops the final e of the infinitive: vendr-.

The main table prints the masculine participle. The feminine cells are the participle list on the same page, joined to the same auxiliary. Vous is êtes allé for one man, êtes allée for one woman, êtes allés for a masculine or mixed group, and êtes allées for a feminine group. The stored 2p cell is the plural masculine that the main table prints. It is not asked.

Le Conjugueur notes the second person plural faites beside nous faisons. The future stem is fer-. The participle agrees when it is a preceding direct object: faite, faits, faites. Those cells are stored and are not asked.

The auxiliary is être, as for aller. The main table prints the masculine participle. Feminine cells are on the same page’s participle list. The future stem is viendr-. Vous follows the same split as aller, and the stored 2p cell is the table’s masculine plural. It is not asked. Venir de plus an infinitive means to have just done, and that construction is not asked.
